podcast.body: This track, critical of radio, was forbidden by NBC executives for Costello's Saturday Night Live performance on December 17, 1977, due to the network's ownership of many radio stations. Despite promising to comply, Costello famously played "Radio, Radio" live, an act of defiance that inspired many. "That other song was a track very critical of radio and since NBC owned a lot of radio stations, no one wanted to risk making the executives with the network angry."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

podcast.body: Elvis Costello was specifically asked by a producer of Saturday Night Live not to play this song during his appearance on December 17, 1978, because NBC, the network, owned many radio stations and the song was considered insulting to radio programmers. Despite the request, he played it anyway, making it a notable incident similar to the Sex Pistols' appearance on Bill Grundy's show. "You can play the show, the producer said, if you promise not to play your song Radio Radio."
